data.gender_notes: Matilde is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Matilde is derived from the Latin name MATIDELIS, composed of MATI- (might) and DE- (battle) meaning 'mighty in battle'. In Christianity, Saint Matilda of Essen is remembered for her charitable deeds. The name Matilde carries the meaning “Mighty in battle” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Matilde usually hope their child will grow to embody mighty in battle and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Matilde
in_english.long_meaning: The name Matilde originates from Germanic roots, signifying 'Strength' and 'Virtue'. In Christian tradition, Matilde is associated with strong personalities, nobility, and courage. It is a popular name across various cultures, symbolizing a strong and virtuous individual. In biblical context, Matilde is not directly mentioned, but its meaning reflects the qualities of a virtuous and noble Christian.

data.cultural_impact: The name Matilde has been popular in various European cultures, especially in Portugal, Spain, Germany, and Italy. In each culture, the name has carried different nuances. In Portugal and Spain, Matilde is is Renaud (Matilde de Carols) was a medieval queen, a member of the House of Bourbon and Duchess of Viseu. In the theater world, Matilda, a musical by Tim Minchin, tells the story of a little girl with telekinesis who, with the assistance of her Lutheran deacon/pork-pie-hat-wearing spiritual advisor, overcomes bullies and assert her independence. Meanwhile, in Italy, Matilde Serao was a highly acclaimed journalist and author. Thus, the name Matilde has been associated with power, achievement, and trailblazing women.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Matilde is rooted in its Latin origins. Matilda, as a warrior name, symbolizes courage and resilience, which are essential traits of the Christian faith. A faithful Christian named Matilde embodies strength in their faith and their resolve to overcome challenges that come their way. In a more spiritual sense, Justina Matilde Blessed Costa, an Italian-Brazilian mystic from the 18th and 19th centuries, had an influential spiritual impact. Her life, characterized by self-denial, love for the Church, deep devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, and the passion to aid the poor and marginalized, is an inspiration for Matildas of all kind. Today, those bearing the name Matilde are called to live their lives with both spiritual and worldly strength, reflecting the beautiful union of our earthly and heavenly journeys.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Matilde: Daughter of might and light, bathed in divine grace. Her name, a testament to strength and courage, illuminates the path for those she leads.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Matilde of Canossa (1046-1111) was an Italian noblewoman and regent of the Duchy of Tuscany. The name Matilde carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
Matilda of Flanders (1050-1083) was the Countess of Flanders and the mother of Philip I, King of France.
